verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere ships a voice-agent/tool-calling stack (RunAnywhere.voice assembling STT+LLM+TTS, and an SDK that 'owns the call-and-execute loop' for registered tools) and an rcli demo that accepts natural-language commands, which is the closest thing to a built-in delegatable assistant. However hands-on community testing directly contradicts reliable delegation: asking rcli to 'navigate to google.com in safari' did nothing while the assistant verbally claimed it had succeeded, a failure the vendor/commenters attribute to small on-device models confusing intent recognition with task completion. Missing for 10: a working, verified end-to-end task-delegation demo, independent corroboration that tool-calling reliably executes real actions, and resolution of the reported segfault/broken-install issues affecting the same CLI.
